coverHeadlines.text: Mira Vale, an instinct for making room
The tiny boat committee meets in these pages
Twenty-five, with clay under her fingernails

openingNote.text: Mira, this issue gathers the small things you do that stay with people: a shelf in order, a detail remembered, a quieter voice invited in. I am proud to be your sister, and I hope your care finds its way back to you.

profile.headline: The care tucked into small details
profile.text: Mira alphabetizes the spice shelf and remembers tiny details people mention once. At a table, she notices who has not found their way into the conversation yet.

featureMemory.headline: A Saturday that turned paper into boats
featureMemory.text: Rain met the Harbor Street book market on a Saturday. When the lights flickered, you carried the paper bags to a window seat at Dot Cafe, split a cinnamon roll, and waited for the rain to clear. Mira folded the empty receipt into tiny boats while you waited. The memory now has a name between you: the tiny boat committee.

dynamicModules.name: The Lore / inside jokes
dynamicModules.headline: Rules for a small boat committee
dynamicModules.text: An empty receipt becomes tiny boats; Saturday begins with the first pancake belonging to its cook, even when it is lopsided. These are your two ordinary-morning rules, and together they can rescue almost any ordinary morning.

dynamicModules.name: Current Obsessions
dynamicModules.headline: The week, in clay and green
dynamicModules.text: Wednesday ceramics at Farrow Studio, tomato pots on the kitchen-window sill, and new songs for Sunday walks make up Mira's current rhythm. The North Loop farmers market is for flowers and a slow weekend start.

whyTheyMatter.headline: Care with follow-through
whyTheyMatter.text: Mira makes room in practical ways: she asks the quieter person a real question, remembers the answer, and calls when she says she will. Her kindness is steady enough that people can lean on it; this is care with follow-through.

currentEra.headline: A present tense made of Wednesdays and walks
currentEra.text: Mira goes to ceramics at Farrow Studio every Wednesday. Tomato pots sit on the kitchen-window sill. She keeps adding songs to the playlist she takes on Sunday walks. At the North Loop farmers market, she likes the flowers and the slow start to the weekend.

birthdayLetter.headline: May your care come back around
birthdayLetter.text: For this birthday, I hope the care you give everyone else finds its way back to you. May 25 bring slow mornings, music for every walk, clay under your fingernails, and room around the table. I am proud to be your sister. I love the life we keep making in small pieces.

backCoverLine.text: Keep making a life in small pieces.
